To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IGF- 1 treatment of primary pulmonary artery endothelial cell cultures increases proliferation and branch points, but not angiogenic protein expression, at the population level.
we have identified a spatially localized cell response to a growth factor treatment in fetal pulmonary endothelial cells using high throughput imaging.
IGF- 1 increases PAEC proliferation and tube formation but does not alter the expression of angiogenic signaling proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new technologies to measure cellular function and the application of these technologies to the study of rare cells in primary cells.
the development of novel methods for high throughput single cell analysis and their application to the discovery of rare cells in primary cell populations.
the spatial and temporal dynamics of cellular responses to external stimuli, and how these responses may differ in healthy and diseased cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IGF- 1 increases the proliferation of PAECs from both healthy and PPHN sheep but does not increase angiogenic signaling proteins or tube formation at the population level.
IGF- 1 treatment increases proliferation and tube formation in PAECs isolated from both healthy and PPHN sheep but that there are spatial and temporal differences in the response to IGF -1.
IGF- 1 increased proliferation, but not angiogenic markers, and increased tube branch points in PAECs isolated from healthy newborn sheep.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
single cell measurements of primary cells are required to fully characterize the response to external stimuli.
cell to cell variability is a fundamental property of primary cells that should be considered when designing in vitro experiments.
the ensemble and non-spatio-temporal single cell assays are not sufficient to fully characterize cellular response to IGF1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
single cell imaging is a powerful tool to understand cell to cell variability that may otherwise be missed using standard in vitro methods.

ensemble and nonspatial readouts applied to populations of primary cells may be misleading due to the presence cell to cell variability, and that single cell imaging can be used to identify and characterize this variability.
single cell imaging is a powerful tool for identifying rare cells that may not be detected with ensemble measurements.
